neighbours.label: atmospheric chemistry and air pollution as the subject of the text
fire: Nitrogen oxides from car exhausts react in sunlight to form ground-level ozone over cities.
Black carbon from diesel engines settles on snow after drifting through the troposphere.
Chlorofluorocarbons slowly rose to the stratosphere, where they thinned the ozone layer.
Regulators tightened limits on soot because smog was shortening lives across the valley.
Volcanic sulfur dioxide forms droplets high up that reflect sunlight back into space.
Coal plants release mercury and acid gases that travel hundreds of miles on the wind.
Atmospheric models show how ammonia from farms turns into haze downwind of the fields.
Greenhouse gases such as nitrous oxide linger in the air for over a century.
quiet: Nitrate fertilizers from farm fields seep through the soil to reach wells under villages.
Plastic fragments from fishing nets settle on the seabed after drifting through the gyre.
Hermit crabs slowly moved to the tide pools, where they found larger shells.
Regulators tightened limits on lead because old pipes were poisoning children across the county.
Volcanic basalt forms columns as it cools, which geologists map along the coast.
Copper mines release tailings and heavy metals that travel hundreds of miles down the river.
Laboratory assays show how enzymes from yeast turn sugar into alcohol inside the vats.
Rare minerals such as monazite remain in the beach sand for a very long time.
